questions.question: In a ΔABC, ∠ABC = 2 ∠CAB, If the side BC is extended to D and ∠ACD = 126°, then ∠CAB is:
questions.solution:
**Given :**

∠ABC = 2 ∠CAB

∠ACD = 126°

**To find :**

∠CAB

**Concept used :**

The Sum of two opposite angles is equal to the exterior angle.

**Calculation :**

Let ∠CAB be x

⇒ ∠ABC = 2x

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba917b6478aa66bec2af858eb834eda51715705f5d4ce60cb870e9a1e15e64ac.png] 

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠CAB = ∠ACD

⇒ 2x + x = 126°

⇒ 3x = 126°

⇒ x = 126°/3

⇒ x = 42°

**∴ ∠CAB is 42°**

questions.question: The compound interest on ₹ 4,000 after 3 year is ₹ 630.50. Then the rate of interest compounded yearly is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs. 4000

Compound Interest = Rs. 630.50

Time = 3 year

**Formula used:**

Compound Interest = Principal[(1 + Rate/100)time – 1]

**Calculation:**

Compound Interest = Principal[(1 + Rate/100)time – 1]

⇒ 630.50 = 4000[(1 + rate/100)³ – 1]

⇒ 630.50/4000 = [(1 + rate/100)³ – 1]

⇒ (1261/8000) + 1 = [(1 + rate/100)³]

⇒ 9261/8000 = [(1 + rate/100)³]

⇒ ∛(9261/8000) = [(1 + rate/100)]

⇒ 21/20 = [(1 + rate/100)]

⇒ 21/20 – 1 = rate/100

⇒ 1/20 = rate/100

⇒ rate = 5%

**∴ The rate of interest compounded yearly is 5%.**43

questions.question: The average marks of Ravi in five subjects are 150, but in mathematics 43 was misread as 23 during the calculation. The correct average is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Correction** = Correct value − Wrong value = 43 − 23 = +20.

Increase in **Average** = Total Correction ÷ Number of subjects = 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

Correct **Average** = Old Average + Increase = 150 + 4 = 154.

**∴ The correct answer is 154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of subjects (n) = 5

Incorrect average = 150

Correct value = 43

Wrong value = 23

**Formula Used:**

Correct Average = (Incorrect Total − Wrong value + Correct value) ÷ n

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c2efb9536c1c97b1b00759a71512d234d40f24d5521992a2b69265a8243d44e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Incorrect sum of marks = 150 × 5 = 750

⇒ Correct sum of marks = 750 − 23 + 43

⇒ Correct sum of marks = 750 + 20 = 770

⇒ Correct average = 770 ÷ 5

⇒ Correct average = 154

**∴ The correct answer is 154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Definition

The average (arithmetic mean) is the ratio of the **sum of observations** to the **total number of observations**. Formula: Average = Σx ÷ n.

Correction in Average

When one or more values are misread, the **Correct Average** = Old Average + [(Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ n].

Weighted Average

Used when different groups have different sizes: **Aw** = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: A circle is with center O. Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn from an external point A. If ∠POQ is equal to 118°. Then find the ∠PAQ:
questions.solution:
**Given :-**

A circle is with center O

Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn from an external point A.

∠POQ = 118°

**Concept :- **

Length of tangents drawn from an outside point to a circle are equal. 

It also makes an quadrilateral. 

In a quadrilateral sum of all angles are 360° 

**Calculation :-**

⇒ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18b1f2b54b4c9271ed113f091bd58a6a52b7cb10150df95d6c59a7ee1cdfa7eb.png] 

⇒ As OP and OQ is radius 

⇒ OP = OQ 

⇒ PA = PQ (From circle properties)

⇒ ∠APO = ∠AQO = 90° (As OP and OQ is perpendicular to PA and AQ)

⇒ Sum of angles = ∠P + ∠O + ∠Q + ∠A 

⇒ 360° = 90° + 118° + 90° + ∠A

⇒ 360° - (90° + 118° + 90°) = ∠A

⇒ 360° - 298° = ∠A

⇒ ∠A = 62° 

⇒ The ∠PAQ = 62° 

**∴ ∠PAQ = 62° **

⇒ Volume of cone = (1/3) × (22/7) × 36 × 7

questions.question: frac{{cos x}}{{1 + sin x}} + frac{{1 + sin x}}{{cos x}} is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To solve trigonometric identities quickly, substitute a specific value for **x**.

Let **x = 0°**: cos 0° = 1 and sin 0° = 0.

Expression = 1 / (1 + 0) + (1 + 0) / 1 = 1 + 1 = **2**.

Now check the options at **x = 0°**:

(1) 2cos 0° = 2, (3) 2sec 0° = 2. Since two options match, test **x = 30°**.

Value at 30° = (√3/2) / (1.5) + (1.5) / (√3/2) = 1/√3 + √3 = 4/√3. Note that **2sec 30° = 4/√3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2sec x.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos x / (1 + sin x) + (1 + sin x) / cos x

**Formula Used:** **sin² x + cos² x = 1** and **sec x = 1 / cos x**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/088b7de57b8ce7f022a8cfce8340ee44a312bb8012cb19cbd4813f60c513bff7.png] 

Take the **LCM** of the denominators (1 + sin x) and cos x:

⇒ [cos x × cos x + (1 + sin x) × (1 + sin x)] / [cos x × (1 + sin x)]

⇒ [cos² x + (1 + sin x)²] / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ [cos² x + 1 + 2sin x + sin² x] / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ [(cos² x + sin² x) + 1 + 2sin x] / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ [1 + 1 + 2sin x] / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ [2 + 2sin x] / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ 2(1 + sin x) / [cos x(1 + sin x)]

⇒ 2 / cos x

⇒ 2sec x

**∴ The correct answer is 2sec x.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

The three fundamental identities are sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Identities

Reciprocal relations include sec θ = 1 / cos θ, cosec θ = 1 / sin θ, and cot θ = 1 / tan θ.

Ratio Identities

Tangent and cotangent can be expressed as ratios: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.</p

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 6 hours and tap B can empty the same tank in 10 hours. If both taps are opened together, then how much time (in hours) will be taken to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total capacity** (LCM of 6 and 10) = 30 units

Efficiency of **Tap A** = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 units/hr (filling)

Efficiency of **Tap B** = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units/hr (emptying)

**Combined efficiency** = 5 − 3 = 2 units/hr

**Time taken** = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time for **Tap A** = 6 hr, Emptying time for **Tap B** = 10 hr.

 
 

 **Tap**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **Tap A** (Fill)
 6
 30 (LCM)
 +5
 
 

 **Tap B** (Empty)
 10
 −3
 
 

⇒ Net efficiency of (**A + B**) per hour = 5 + (−3) = 2 units/hr

⇒ Total **capacity** of the tank = 30 units

⇒ **Time taken** to fill the tank = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 15 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its work done in 1 hour is 1/x. If an **outlet pipe** empties it in y hours, its work done in 1 hour is −1/y.

Direct Formula for Two Pipes

When one pipe fills (x) and another empties (y), the time taken to fill the tank is given by T = (x × y) ÷ (y − x), where y > x.

Negative Work Concept

An **emptying tap** performs negative work. Its efficiency is always subtracted from the filling efficiency to find the **net rate**.</p

questions.question: In a class, if 60% of the students are boys and the number of girls is 36, then the number of boys is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 60% : 40% = 3 : 2.

Given: 2 units (**Girls**) = 36.

1 unit = 18.

3 units (**Boys**) = 18 × 3 = 54.

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Percentage of boys** = 60%

**Number of girls** = 36

**Formula Used:**

**Total Percentage** = 100%

**Number of boys** = (Percentage of boys ÷ Percentage of girls) × Number of girls

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98f6998d8bf4e85c7c2ce0a1665087dddd8d39af76854b20da0d3e584c70cafe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Percentage of girls** = 100% − 60% = 40%

⇒ Let the **Total number of students** be 'x'.

⇒ 40% of x = 36

⇒ (40 ÷ 100) × x = 36

⇒ x = (36 × 100) ÷ 40

⇒ x = 90

⇒ **Number of boys** = 60% of 90

⇒ **Number of boys** = (60 ÷ 100) × 90 = 54

**∴ The correct answer is 54.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To solve quickly, use fractions: 60% = 3/5 and 40% = 2/5. If 2/5 of total = 36, then 1/5 = 18 and 3/5 = 54.

Base Value Rule

Always identify the base (100%) which represents the **total number of students** in such problems.

Ratio Application

When percentages sum to 100, the ratio of parts can be used directly: **Boys : Girls** = 60 : 40 = 3 : 2.</p

questions.question: If a and b are two positive real numbers such that a + b = 20 and ab = 4, then the value of a³ + b³ is:

⇒ a3 + b³ = 20 × (20² – 12)

⇒ a3 + b³ = 20 × (400 – 12)

⇒ a3 + b³ = 20 × 388

⇒ a3 + b³ = 7760

questions.question: The area of a rectangle is a² - b² and its length is a + b, what will be its breadth?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The area of a rectangle is a2 - b2 and its length is a + b. We have to find the breadth of the rectangle

**Concept Used:**

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

a2 - b² = (a + b)(a - b)

**Calculation:**

The area of a rectangle is a2 - b2 

Its length is a + b

Area of a rectangle = Length × Breadth

⇒ a2 - b2 = (a + b) × Breadth

⇒ (a + b)(a - b) = (a + b) × Breadth

⇒ Breadth = (a - b)

**∴ Its breadth will be (a - b)**
